earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 a991pressrelease93026.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 The Travelers Companies, Inc. 485 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017-2630 www.travelers.com NYSE: TRV Travelers Reports Excellent Third Quarter and Year-to-Date Results Third Quarter 2026 Net Income per Diluted Share of $9.04 and Core Income per Diluted Share of $9.18 Third Quarter 2026 Return on Equity of 24.7% and Core Return on Equity of 22.1% • Third quarter net income of $1.917 billion and core income of $1.947 billion. • Underwriting income of $1.432 billion pre-tax and underlying underwriting income of $1.736 billion pre-tax. • Strong margins with a consolidated combined ratio of 86.8% and underlying combined ratio of 84.1%. • Net favorable prior year reserve development in all three segments totaled $234 million pre-tax. • Net written premiums of $11.480 billion. • Record net investment income of $1.098 billion pre-tax ($908 million after-tax) increased 6%. • Total capital of $1.769 billion returned to shareholders, including $1.508 billion of share repurchases. New York, October 16, 2026 — The Travelers Companies, Inc. today reported net income of $1.917 billion, or $9.04 per diluted share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.888 billion, or $8.24 per diluted share, in the prior year quarter. Core income in the current quarter was $1.947 billion, or $9.18 per diluted share, compared to $1.867 billion, or $8.14 per diluted share, in the prior year quarter. Core income increased primarily due to higher net favorable prior year reserve development and higher net investment income, partially offset by higher catastrophe losses. Net realized investment losses in the current quarter were $34 million pre-tax ($30 million after-tax), compared to net realized investment gains of $27 million pre-tax ($21 million after-tax) in the prior year quarter. Per diluted share amounts benefited from the impact of share repurchases. Consolidated Highlights ($ in millions, except for per share amounts, and after-tax, except for premiums and revenues) Three Months Ended September 30, Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 2025 Change 2026 2025 Change Net written premiums $ 11,480 $ 11,473 — % $ 33,347 $ 33,531 (1) % Total revenues $ 12,412 $ 12,470 — $ 36,489 $ 36,396 — Net income $ 1,917 $ 1,888 2 $ 5,836 $ 3,792 54 per diluted share $ 9.04 $ 8.24 10 $ 27.05 $ 16.45 64 Core income $ 1,947 $ 1,867 4 $ 5,803 $ 3,814 52 per diluted share $ 9.18 $ 8.14 13 $ 26.90 $ 16.54 63 Diluted weighted average shares outstanding 210.6 227.5 (7) 214.2 228.9 (6) Combined ratio 86.8 % 87.3 % (0.5) pts 86.3 % 93.2 % (6.9) pts Underlying combined ratio 84.1 % 83.9 % 0.2 pts 84.5 % 84.4 % 0.1 pts Return on equity 24.7 % 24.7 % — pts 24.3 % 17.3 % 7.0 pts Core return on equity 22.1 % 22.6 % (0.5) pts 22.3 % 15.8 % 6.5 pts As of Change From September 30, 2026 December 31, 2025 September 30, 2025 December 31, 2025 September 30, 2025 Book value per share $ 141.48 $ 151.21 $ 141.72 (6) % — % Adjusted book value per share 172.47 158.01 150.55 9 % 15 % See Glossary of Financial Measures for definitions and the statistical supplement for additional financial data. 1 “We are pleased to report excellent third quarter results,” said Alan Schnitzer, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. “It was another in a run of successful quarters, with very strong underwriting performance across all three segments and a record result from our investment portfolio. Core income for the quarter was $1.9 billion, or $9.18 per diluted share. Core return on equity for the quarter was 22.1%, bringing core return on equity over the last four quarters to 24.1%. Third quarter underwriting income of $1.4 billion pre-tax benefited from continued strong levels of underlying underwriting income and net favorable prior year development. Profitability was excellent on both a reported and underlying basis. The combined ratio improved to 86.8%, and the underlying combined ratio remained very strong at 84.1%. “Our high-quality investment portfolio generated after-tax net investment income of $908 million, an increase of 7%. These results, along with our exceptionally strong balance sheet, enabled us to return $1.8 billion of excess capital to our shareholders during the quarter, including $1.5 billion of share repurchases. “Through disciplined marketplace execution across all three segments, we generated net written premiums in the quarter of $11.5 billion. In Business Insurance, we grew in every line other than Property, generating net written premiums of $5.9 billion, up 4% from the prior year quarter adjusting for the sale of our Canadian businesses. Renewal premium change in the segment was 4.1%, including renewal premium change of 5.4% in our core Middle Market business and 7.8% in our small commercial Select business. Excluding the Property line, renewal premium change in the segment was 7.0%. Retention remained very strong at 86% and was higher or stable in every line. Renewal premium change was by and large orderly and when viewed together with retention and returns reflects excellent execution. New business was a third quarter record at $699 million, up 4% over the prior year quarter. “In Bond & Specialty Insurance, we grew net written premiums by 12% to $1.2 billion. In our high-quality Management Liability business renewal premium change improved sequentially to 3.8% while retention remained steady at an excellent 89%. New business in the segment was up 18% over the prior year quarter. In our leading Surety business, we grew net written premiums by 21%, reflecting continued strong production across the portfolio. “In Personal Insurance, we generated net written premiums of $4.4 billion, with solid retention in both Auto and Homeowners and higher new business in our Homeowners business. “Our strong underwriting and investment results through the first nine months of the year reflect the strength of our franchise. We are well positioned to finish the year strong. That momentum, and the advances we are making on our innovation agenda, give us real confidence heading into 2027 and beyond.” 2 Consolidated Results Three Months Ended September 30, Nine Months Ended September 30, ($ in millions and pre-tax, unless noted otherwise) 2026 2025 Change 2026 2025 Change Underwriting gain: $ 1,432 $ 1,378 $ 54 $ 4,343 $ 2,095 $ 2,248 Underwriting gain includes : Net favorable prior year reserve development 234 22 212 1,225 715 510 Catastrophes, net of reinsurance (538) (402) (136) (1,817) (3,595) 1,778 Net investment income 1,098 1,033 65 3,176 2,905 271 Other income (expense), including interest expense (127) (94) (33) (339) (279) (60) Core income before income taxes 2,403 2,317 86 7,180 4,721 2,459 Income tax expense 456 450 6 1,377 907 470 Core income 1,947 1,867 80 5,803 3,814 1,989 Net realized investment gains (losses) after income taxes (30) 21 (51) 33 (22) 55 Net income $ 1,917 $ 1,888 $ 29 $ 5,836 $ 3,792 $ 2,044 Combined ratio 86.8 % 87.3 % (0.5) pts 86.3 % 93.2 % (6.9) pts Impact on combined ratio Net favorable prior year reserve development (2.1) pts (0.2) pts (1.9) pts (3.8) pts (2.2) pts (1.6) pts Catastrophes, net of reinsurance 4.8 pts 3.6 pts 1.2 pts 5.6 pts 11.0 pts (5.4) pts Underlying combined ratio 84.1 % 83.9 % 0.2 pts 84.5 % 84.4 % 0.1 pts Net written premiums Business Insurance $ 5,868 $ 5,675 3 % $ 17,638 $ 17,165 3 % Bond & Specialty Insurance 1,209 1,080 12 3,512 3,164 11 Personal Insurance 4,403 4,718 (7) 12,197 13,202 (8) Total $ 11,480 $ 11,473 — % $ 33,347 $ 33,531 (1) % Third Quarter 2026 Results (All comparisons vs. third quarter 2025, unless noted otherwise) Net income of $1.917 billion increased $29 million, driven by higher core income, partially offset by net realized investment losses compared to net realized investment gains in the prior year quarter. Net realized investment losses were $34 million pre-tax ($30 million after-tax), compared to net realized investment gains of $27 million pre-tax ($21 million after-tax) in the prior year quarter. Year-to-Date 2026 Results (All comparisons vs. year-to-date 2025, unless noted otherwise) Net income of $5.836 billion increased $2.044 billion, driven by higher core income and net realized investment gains compared to net realized investment losses in the prior year period. Core income of $5.803 billion increased $1.989 billion, primarily due to lower catastrophe losses, higher net favorable prior year reserve development and higher net investment income. Net realized investment gains were $75 million pre-tax ($33 million after-tax), compared to net realized investment losses of $28 million pre-tax ($22 million after-tax) in the prior year period. Combined ratio: • The combined ratio of 86.3% improved 6.9 points due to lower catastrophe losses (5.4 points) and higher net favorable prior year reserve development (1.6 points), partially offset by a higher underlying combined ratio (0.1 points). • The underlying combined ratio was an excellent 84.5%. See below for further details by segment. • Net favorable prior year reserve development occurred in all segments. Net investment income of $3.176 billion pre-tax ($2.624 billion after-tax) increased 9%, driven by the same factors described above for the third quarter of 2026. Net written premiums of $33.347 billion decreased 1%. Net written premiums in the prior year period included $736 million related to the Canadian operations which the Company divested in the first quarter of 2026. Excluding the impact of the sale, net written premiums increased 2% over the prior year period. See below for further details by segment. Shareholders’ Equity Shareholders’ equity of $28.995 billion decreased 12% from year-end 2025, primarily due to higher net unrealized investment losses, common share repurchases and dividends to shareholders, partially offset by net income of $5.836 billion. Net unrealized investment losses included in shareholders’ equity were $8.049 billion pre-tax ($6.352 billion after-tax), compared to $1.862 billion pre-tax ($1.478 billion after-tax) at year-end 2025. The increase in net unrealized investment losses was driven by higher interest rates. Book value per share of $141.48 decreased 6% from year-end 2025. reference.summary: The Travelers Companies, Inc., through its subsidiaries, provides a range of commercial and personal property, and casualty insurance products and services to businesses, government units, associations, and individuals in the United States, Canada, and internationally. It operates through three segments: Business Insurance, Bond & Specialty Insurance, and Personal Insurance. The Business Insurance segment offers workers' compensation, commercial automobile and property, general liability, commercial multi-peril, employers' liability, public and product liability, professional indemnity, marine, aviation, commercial property and automobile, onshore and offshore energy, construction, terrorism, personal accident, and kidnap and ransom insurance products.
